desktop.methodology: Median warm time per entry after symmetric 1.5×IQR outlier filtering; raw samples and exclusions are retained. Each runtime warms for at least 150 ms, calibrates a batch, then measures the recorded number of batches. Every timed return-value checksum is verified. Printed output is verified before timing; timed output uses a null sink (native) or byte callback (web). Formatting and runtime-specific I/O remain included. Includes the host call boundary and budget reset where required; excludes loading, process startup, downloads and offline compilation. Tiny examples emphasize call overhead. Host gate: every measured job runs pinned (inherited affinity, no wrapper) to one logical CPU of the quietest core, chosen again before each attempt once its other hyperthread has settled, and is repeated unless that CPU kept its clock within 3% of the job median (10th to 90th percentile), the median reached 95% of the clock calibrated at start, and the hyperthread sibling was busy at most 15% of the job; Go runs with GOMAXPROCS=1 on that CPU. Rejected attempts are retained with their observations.

methodology: Median whole-process wall time after one discarded warmup; shuffled execution order; symmetric 1.5×IQR outliers excluded, raw samples retained. C: cc -O2; Go: go build; ZX: the instruction engine (zi2zx run); Native: zi2zx then zx2native; WebAssembly: zi2zx then zx2wasm, run by Node including engine startup, compilation and instantiation. Emission includes loading, checking, linking and writing output; it excludes downstream C/Go builds. Output size is emitted files, including C headers, rather than linked executables. Shared host, warm filesystem caches, no CPU isolation. Small examples emphasize startup; these are not language rankings.
